correctness.rationale: The required q-run lower bound follows from the q distinct unique letter factors, and q last-in-run positions suffice. For any q-position selection, every consecutive two-letter factor has precisely one occurrence, forcing the last-left or first-right condition, and all other factors are covered if these conditions hold. Singleton separators factor choices; each non-singleton block has t+1 endpoint configurations or one strictly internal selection at a run, yielding 1+sum(a_i-1). Explicit block generating functions simplify to the rational census, and coefficient extraction is binomial. Definition-level checks passed on 339 vectors/6786 selections and 54 composition coefficient pairs. Formal algebra checked; finite experiments are not a universal proof.

The closest inspected full texts study binary morphic families, generic concatenation inequalities, and general infinite-word behavior rather than this same domain. Published-research-record searches found no equivalent statement, subject to residual unindexed-equivalence risk. A previous own repeated-permutation attractor result does not cover single-occurrence-per-symbol runs.

value.rationale: The fine-grained multiplicity of smallest attractors is a natural combinatorial invariant emphasized as an open avenue in Banbara et al. CPM 2026. This theorem supplies a complete all-parameter classification for a canonical run-length class (pairwise distinct symbols, arbitrary positive run lengths), a meaningful structural singleton-separator factorization and exact length/alphabet-size census. Unlike a single easy q lower bound, it determines all optimal hitting sets and multiplicities; applications beyond this class are not asserted.
